$comment: Vendor-engine exceptions for the TASK-OSS-P5-03 browser matrix. An entry removes one {engine, condition} cell from the lane and MUST say why, at which engine version it was observed, and when it was last re-checked. A blanket skip is not an exception -- it is the lane narrowing without saying so, which is the failure this file exists to prevent.
method: Each {engine, condition} pair was opened with the context options the matrix uses, and the corresponding media query was read back from the page. See the handoff in docs/program-2026-08/EXECUTION-STATUS.md.

chromium.touch: (pointer: coarse) resolves true with hasTouch + isMobile

firefox.touch: (pointer: coarse) resolves true with hasTouch + isMobile -- isMobile IS accepted at 1.61.1, contrary to older guidance

webkit.forced-colors: (forced-colors: active) resolves true -- forcedColors IS accepted at 1.61.1, contrary to older guidance. Note this emulates the media feature; it does not install a system palette, so a spec must assert that an indicator survives rather than that it takes a system color.
webkit.touch: (pointer: coarse) resolves true with hasTouch + isMobile

reCheckedResult: All 12 {engine, condition} pairs for firefox and webkit were re-measured on Windows at Playwright 1.61.1 by creating the context the matrix creates and reading the media feature back. All 12 resolve as recorded on 2026-08-24, so the Linux-derived guidance the 2026-08-24 note contradicts is still contradicted on Windows: webkit accepts forcedColors and firefox accepts isMobile. Both engines then executed all six conditions against all 88 runnable targets. `exceptions` stays EMPTY: not one {engine, condition} pair had to be removed from the lane.

engineBehaviours.behaviour: WebKit keeps CSS animations in playState "running" on elements inside a `display: none` subtree. CSS Animations Level 1 states that setting `display` to `none` "will terminate any running animation applied to the element and its descendants"; chromium 149 and firefox 151 terminate, webkit 26.5 does not. Measured directly: Storybook's own `.sb-preparing-story > .sb-loader` spinner (an infinite `sb-rotate360` animation, hidden with `display: none` once the story is shown but never removed from the DOM) is reported as running by webkit and by neither other engine. `document.getAnimations()` -> 1 running on webkit, 0 on chromium, 0 on firefox, for the same page at the same moment.
engineBehaviours.impactBeforeFix: 84 of 88 Tier B-D components failed matrix-webkit-reduced-motion naming DIV.sb-loader. Not one named an element the component rendered.
engineBehaviours.resolution: NOT an exception -- the condition is measurable on webkit once the assertion stops counting elements with no box. `e2e/matrix/conditions.spec.ts` now filters `getAnimations()` on `node.isConnected && node.checkVisibility()` (supported by all three engines). After the fix: webkit 176/176, firefox 176/176, chromium 176/176 on reduced-motion. Removing the {webkit, reduced-motion} cell from the lane instead would have hidden every real reduced-motion defect on that engine.
engineBehaviours.upstreamIssueNote: No upstream WebKit bug id was verified from this offline environment; the normative spec sentence is cited instead. Confirming or filing one is an owner action (N1-O2 handoff, D5).
